title: Architecture plan
description: How the analysed reference maps onto GraphCompose, at examples/<project>/revisions/<id>/architecture-plan.json. The load-bearing part is componentMapping: region -> named render method -> primitives, which is what makes selective rollback and per-region review possible at all. architecture-plan.md keeps the reasoning, the risks and the layer-split narrative. Primitives named here must exist in the pinned skill pack's API allow-list — the plan is not the place to invent GraphCompose APIs.

schemaVersion.description: On-disk contract version for this artifact.

targetGraphComposeVersion.description: GraphCompose version this plan targets. Must agree with targetGraphComposeVersion in revision.json.

lane.description: Which upstream template generation this document kind sits on. Per AGENTS.md: cv and coverletter are V2 layered, proposal is V2 single-preset, invoice is V1 classic.

documentKind.description: Canonical document kind. "other" still routes through the same primitive-level pipeline; only the published-bundle factory cares about the kind.

upstreamCheatsheet.description: The upstream authoring document this plan follows, e.g. docs/templates/v2-layered/authoring-presets.md.

componentMapping.description: One entry per visual region. This is the spine of the whole contract: visual-review.json reports mismatches against these component names, changedComponents in revision.json lists them, and selective rollback restores them one at a time.

renderMethod.description: Named private render method that owns the region, e.g. "renderHeader". Every visible region maps to exactly one, which is what makes component-level rollback work.

primitives.description: GraphCompose primitives the method reaches for, e.g. ["RowBuilder.weights", "LayerStackBuilder.position"]. Must appear in the pinned skill pack's allow-list.

baseConstants.description: The small set of constants every derived dimension comes from. Relational geometry means widths and weights are derived from these; a hardcoded pixel value belongs here only when the dimension is genuinely independent (icon size, marker height, fixed padding).

derivation.description: How dependent dimensions are derived from this constant. Absent means the constant is independent.

themeTokens.description: Theme-level tokens, the surface a theme-only revision is allowed to touch.

role.description: Colour role or type-scale role this token fills, from visual-analysis.json.

selectedSkills.description: Skill ids from skills/skill-manifest.json this plan relies on. With progressive disclosure these are the files the coder is expected to have read.

layerSplit.description: V2 layered lane only: what this revision puts in each layer. Omit for the V1 classic lane.

widgetReuseAudit.description: V2 layered lane only: for each visual need, whether an existing widget covers it. A NEW verdict without a justification is what this audit exists to prevent.

need.description: The visual region or element that needs a widget.

justification.description: Required when the verdict is new.

dataFile.description: The <doc-kind>-data.json the template renders from. Content literals must not live in the Java body.

dataModel.description: The data-spec contract. data-schema.md documents the fields; this records where they live.

visualRisks.description: What is most likely to come out wrong on the first render. skills/workflows/create-template/SKILL.md forbids skipping this.

knownLimitations.description: What the plan knowingly cannot reproduce, and what it is betting on. A @Beta surface must record which one, the version it was verified against, and the migration risk on the next minor bump.

notes.description: Prose the rest of this schema cannot carry — a table comparing revisions, a paragraph of causal reasoning — emitted verbatim by scripts/render-artifact-md.mjs under a Notes heading. Markdown blocks. This exists so the reading copy stays generated: narrative belongs here, not in a hand-written .md twin that can disagree with this file.

pagination.description: How the document is paginated. Required once the reference has more than one page, and checked by check-region-primitives: a multi-page document built without deciding this first gets its page model by accident. A book's first page is not its second — different margins, no running header, often no page number — and DocumentSession.pageMargins takes per-page rules (PageMarginRule.page(1, ...)) precisely so that can be stated rather than worked around.

pageModel.description: uniform: every page shares margins and chrome. first-page-different: page 1 has its own margins or chrome (a cover, a title page, a letterhead) — say what differs in firstPageDiffers. sectioned: distinct runs of pages, each with its own model, separated by explicit breaks.

firstPageDiffers.description: What page 1 does that the rest do not, e.g. "zero margins for a full-bleed cover", "no running header", "no page number". Required when pageModel is first-page-different.

pageMarginRules.description: The PageMarginRule entries the template passes to DocumentSession.pageMargins, as written.

breaks.description: Explicit page breaks (AbstractFlowBuilder.addPageBreak). A break the layout needs and nobody declared is a break that moves whenever the content does.

rule.description: keepTogether: this block must not be split across a page break. keepWithNext: it must not be the last thing on a page — a heading orphaned above its content, a table header alone at the foot.

keepRules.description: Where the flow must not break, decided before the layout is built. A document that only ever renders its one-page sample never exercises a break, so these are not discoverable from the render — they are read off the reference and the content that will fill it.

allOf.description: The layered lanes are the ones that have layers to split; V1 classic has none.
